agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19 and pursuant to the AB361. All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll
call vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. The meeting will be live streamed at
https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to bayala@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may also speak
during the meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before
the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the
Zoom conference to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency. In order
to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the Commission meeting will be open and public but conducted
virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. This
way, the public, the staff, and the Commission will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
agenda, but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission
and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.
Members of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests
that you sign up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be
present in the Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions
for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
 Public Works Commission  Page 3 of 3  December 13, 2023

meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or
abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent
Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public
speakers shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the
rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the Public Works Department, and available upon request by emailing bayala@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental
Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted in
accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 8th day of December 2023, at 3:00 p.m.

Date prepared:  December 6, 2023  Meeting date: December 13, 2023

Subject:  2015 Pacific Coast Highway Safety Study Update

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file an update on the project recommendations
in the 2015 Pacific Coast Highway Safety Study.

DISCUSSION: Approved by the City Council on June 22, 2015, the 2015 Pacific Coast
Highway Safety Study focused on evaluating road conditions, identifying accident trends,
examining traffic conflicts, and devising strategies to enhance safety for all PCH. This
comprehensive study culminated in a set of project recommendations aimed at improving
safety on PCH.

The study recommended 130 safety projects. These projects were listed in priority order
based upon the analysis conducted in the study. Since its approval, the City has been
steadily working on these recommendations in an effort to improve safety on PCH. The
following is a summary of the progress the City has made on the safety recommendations:

Projects in the Construction Phase
Presently, the City has two major projects in the construction phase:

  1. PCH Signal Synchronization Project (Priority #1,16, 29, 46, 47, 48, 53, 56, 80,
  81, 82, 87, 88, 117) – This project includes the upgrade of the traffic signals from
  Topanga Canyon Road to John Tyler Drive. The project will synchronize all the
  traffic signals in the project limits including new closed-circuit cameras at each
  intersection and replace existing signal poles. The project will also include street
  improvements with ADA upgrades and install changeable message signs. Mid-block
  sensors will allow Caltrans to capture traffic data, including flow and speed, then
  remotely adjust signal timing in the moment. The project will enhance and improve
  traffic signals which will reduce overall traffic congestion, traffic flow and safety for

   all modes of travel. This project is currently under construction and is expected to
  be completed in Spring 2025.
  2. PCH Median Improvements – John Tyler Drive to Puerco Canyon Road – This
  project includes refurbishing the existing medians on PCH from John Tyler Drive to
  Puerco Canyon Road. The center of the medians will be upgraded with new
  stamped concrete. This project is anticipated to be under construction within the
  next few months and will take approximately 6 months to complete.

Projects in the Design Phase
The City has recently identified funding (Metro Measure R and M) and is proceeding with
the design of the following projects:

  1. PCH Intersection Improvements – Trancas Canyon Road (Priority #22, 70, 71)
  – This project includes the installation of a new dedicated west bound right turn lane
  on PCH. This project is currently in the review stage with Caltrans. The City expects
  that this approval process will be completed within the next three months. This
  project will likely commence once the Trancas Creek Bridge replacement is
  completed.
  2. PCH Pedestrian Undercrossing at Malibu Seafood (Priority #78) – This project
  includes the installation of a new pedestrian undercrossing adjacent to the Puerco
  Canyon Creek and Malibu Seafood. This project will improve safety on PCH by
  creating a safe path of travel for pedestrians who seek to cross PCH.
  3. PCH Median Improvements at Paradise Cove and Zuma Beach (Priority #4, 10,
  129) – This project consists of constructing raised medians at Paradise Cove
  intersection and near Zuma Beach area, relocating a bus stop and new signage.
  4. PCH at Las Flores and Rambla Pacifico Intersection Improvements (Priority
  #58, 59, 61, 62, 63, 64, 91, 92, 93, 116, 126) – The project scope includes a full
  analysis and evaluation to reconfigure and design these intersections to improve
  safety.
  5. PCH Crosswalk Improvements at Big Rock Drive and 20326 PCH (Priority #7,
  15, 32, 65, 66, 67, 94) – The project will include constructing raised medians near
  the Big Rock Drive intersection, installing new flashing warning beacons near 20326
  PCH and overhead warning “signal ahead” beacons near the Big Rock Drive
  intersection.

Projects in the Planning Phase
The following projects were identified in the City’s 2023-2028 Five Year Capital
Improvement Plan. These projects are planned to be implemented in Fiscal Years 2025-
2028 or if funding and resources become available sooner. Once funding has been
identified, staff will proceed with the design and construction of these projects:

  1. PCH Signal Synchronization Project – John Tyler to Trancas Canyon Rd
  (Priority #2) – This project is the second phase to interconnect the existing traffic
  signal system from John Tyler to Trancas Canyon Rd.
  2. PCH Improvements at Paradise Cove (Priority #24) – The project will include
  installing a new eastbound right turn lane onto Paradise Cove, widen the shoulder

  Page 2 of 4
  Agenda Item # 4.A.
   on the inland side of PCH, construct a sidewalk behind the shoulder and modify the
  signal phasing.
  3. Right-turn Extension at PCH and Morning View Dr (Priority #37) – The project
  will consist of extending the existing right turn lane at PCH and Morning View Dr.
  This will allow morning and afternoon school traffic to enter into the right turn lane
  and avoid blocking the No. 2 travel lane on PCH.
  4. PCH Improvements at Heathercliff Rd (Priority #23, 39, 40) – This project will
  include increasing the storage length of the westbound left turn lane, and installing
  a new center median between Portshead Rd. to Heathercliff Rd.

Additional Tasks
The following tasks are not necessarily identified in a specific Capital Improvement Project.
However, the City will be working on these tasks within this upcoming year.

  1. Evaluate vehicle speeds to determine if a lower speed limit is warranted (Priority
  #35)
  2. Replace blue side-street name signs that intersect PCH with larger letters or
  advanced street name signs at prominent intersections (Priority #68)
  3. Install streetlights at identified locations; Guernsey Ave, Latigo Canyon Rd., near
  El Pescador Beach, Encinal Canyon Rd., El Matador Beach, Lunita Rd., Latigo
  Shores Dr., Escondido Beach Rd. (Priority #72, 76, 99, 100, 101, 102, 105, 106)
  4. Install or relocate bus stops at identified locations; near Kanan Dume Dr., Webb
  Way, and Malibu Canyon Rd. (Priority #74, 84)
  5. Consider realignment of Encinal Canyon Road at the intersection of PCH and La
  Pierda Beach Rd including whether a roundabout would be appropriate (Priority
  #130)
  6. Consider realigning Malibu Road with PCH (Priority #124)

Completed Projects and Tasks
Since the completion of the 2015 PCH Safety Study, the City has completed 7 of the 130
recommendations. The following is a list of the completed projects and tasks.

  1. PCH Parking Study (Priority #9)
  2. PCH at La Costa Pedestrian Improvements (Priority #30)
  3. PCH at Kanan Dume Intersection Improvements and Arrester Bed (Priority #41)
  4. PCH at Big Rock Drive Intersection Improvements (Priority #95, 96)
  5. Increase law enforcement efforts (Priority #8)
  6. Consider installing a roundabout at Civic Center Way and Webb Way (Priority #85)

 On November 14, 2023, staff, elected officials, and key stakeholders attended the PCH
Task Force meeting where the community was able to discuss their concerns regarding
the current safety conditions on PCH. Following this, Caltrans organized a Road Safety
Audit on November 28, 2023, to walk the area on PCH from Las Flores Canyon Road to
the Malibu Pier and to identify safety deficiencies. Staff, along with representatives of the
LA County Sheriff’s Department, participated with Caltrans on the Road Safety Audit.
Caltrans will be preparing a draft and final Road Safety Report that will include their
findings and recommendations.

Staff held a follow-up meeting on December 5th with Caltrans to discuss the remaining
PCH Safety Study recommended safety projects. The City and Caltrans identified which
agency will be taking the lead on initiating the specific recommendations. Staff has been
collaborating with Caltrans on a regular basis in an effort to implement these project
recommendations.
